request: Review every registered rule for useful coverage improvements without increasing known false positives.
methodology: Enumerate the live catalog, source-owned summary, limitations and authored examples for every rule.

Exercise every authored example and CRLF form; additionally use scope-aware TypeScript import aliases and static bracket members, safe Python import aliases and AST formatting, and SQL token reflow. Formatting-sensitive policies are not reformatted.

The probe scaffolds include project metadata, real Zod declarations, and explicit documented configuration for opt-in restrictions. Canonical temporary paths preserve local-source provenance checks on macOS.
Unknown TypeScript member names, source masking, foreign interface names, malformed/compound HCL and SQL dialect guards are retained as negative boundaries.
Focused regressions were red before implementation; the complete package suites, suppression/precedence/autofix suites, dogfood, type checking and make verify are the final gate.
Only the 36 demonstrated owning-rule changes are shipped; no rule is added or promoted and no consumer tree is modified.

admission.observableFailure: Equivalent static API spellings evade existing detectors or validation exemptions; multiline SQL and parenthesized HCL cross token boundaries; aliases hide visible Python service interfaces; undefined grouping suggestions can change absence semantics.
admission.owner: Existing language rules and their native parsers; @typescript-eslint ASTUtils.getPropertyName supplies maintained static-member resolution.
admission.harm: Existing SQL/security/correctness policies can be bypassed by equivalent spelling, while already-valid aliases, zoned timestamps and absent-property checks can receive misleading diagnostics.
admission.upstreamReview: Reuse existing Sarj owners and the maintained upstream AST utility. Existing rules retain their narrow local policy, so no new configurable blanket ban is introduced.
admission.smallestFix: Resolve static syntax at existing matching boundaries; preserve provenance, scope, masking and opt-in policy; omit undefined grouping candidates.

corpusInspection.selection: Inspect every newly introduced diagnostic through the bounded private report; unchanged diagnostics retain their earlier calibration.
scopeNotes: Private identities, revisions, content hashes and snippets remain in owner-readable overlays. Four stale existing private pins were excluded rather than refreshed.
Opt-in storage/library policies are configured in labeled probes; default corpus policy leaves them disabled.
Type-required rules are covered by typed labeled probes and package tests; syntax-only corpus evaluation does not establish their type-dependent recall.
Public corpus diversity is limited to Standards; consumer snapshots include explicit SQL and Terraform subsets. Authored examples and package tests separately cover Terraform test-oracle positives.
Natural findings are policy advisories; labeled match counts are not an estimate of precision on arbitrary code.

performance.method: Three alternating pairs, each in fresh processes, on deterministic 100-file public subsets. First-run and warm samples are retained; OS caches were not flushed. Python records peak RSS; TypeScript records RSS at worker completion. Combined Python uses all 135 Python rules on the Python subset; combined TypeScript uses syntax-compatible rules, excluding five rules that require type services. Concurrent validation limits timing precision; no speedup is claimed.
